item.description:
18 DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE AND FINANCIAL SERVICES
125 MAINE REVENUE SERVICES
Chapter 302: SALES TO GOVERNMENTAL AGENCIES AND EXEMPT ORGANIZATIONS
SUMMARY: Establishes administrative rules regarding tax-exempt sales and explains the circumstances under which a retailer or service provider will be relieved of its burden of proving that sales to an entity described in 36 M.R.S. §§ 1760 or 2557, including an agency or instrumentality of the federal government or of the State of Maine, are exempt from Maine sales, or use, or service provider tax.
SECTION 1. Exempt sales generally; burden of proof 1. Generally Sales and Use Tax. Sales to certain organizations and governmental agencies are exempt from sales and use tax pursuant to 36 M.R.S. § 1760. Pursuant to 36 M.R.S. § 1760-C, an exemption provided by 36 M.R.S. § 1760 to a person based upon its charitable, nonprofit , or other public purposes applies only if the property or service purchased is intended to be used by the person primarily in the activity identified by the particular exemption. The burden of proving a sale is to an organization that is exempt under 36 M.R.S. § 1760 is on the person making the sale. The retailer is relieved of this burden of proof if it satisfies the provisions of this rule. 2. Certain purchases subject to tax. Pursuant to 36 M.R.S. § 1760- C, an exemption provided by 36 M.R.S. § 1760 to a person based upon its charitable, nonprofit, or other public purposes applies only if the property or taxable service purchased is intended to be used by the person primarily in the activity identified by the particular exemption. If property or taxable services that were purchased exempt are used primarily in an activity or activities not identified by the particular exemption, use tax liability accrues. Upcoming Federal Changes to MaineCare Eligibility for Some Non-citizens

Aug 20, 2026

We are writing to inform you about an upcoming change to MaineCare eligibility that may affect some of your MaineCare patients. This change is required by federal legislation signed into law in July 2025 (also called H.R.1, One Big Beautiful Bill, P.L.119-21, or Working Families Tax Cuts Act) that made changes to the Medicaid program nationally. These changes apply in all states, including Maine.

Beginning October 1, 2026, MaineCare eligibility is changing for some noncitizen groups. As a result, some individuals who currently receive full MaineCare benefits will no longer qualify for full coverage and will instead be eligible only for Emergency Services MaineCare. An explanation of covered benefits under Emergency Services MaineCare is available in the MaineCare Benefits Manual, Chapter 1, Section 1.02-4(D).

These changes will not affect children under age 21, or pregnant individuals through 12 months after the end of their pregnancy. Please note that the Office for Family Independence (OFI) is still completing the state rulemaking process to implement these federal requirements.

What You Should Know:

  • The eligibility changes are expected to take effect on October 1, 2026.
  • Members who are affected will receive a formal Notice of Decision from OFI before any eligibility changes take place. These notices are expected to be mailed in September 2026.
  • Some members received an early awareness letter in June or July 2026 to let them know they may be affected. This letter was informational only and is not an eligibility determination.

How You Can Help:

As a trusted healthcare provider, you can play an important role in helping your patients prepare for these changes by:

  • Encouraging patients to read any letters they receive from MaineCare or OFI.
  • Reminding patients to report any changes to their immigration status to OFI if it has changed since May 2026, as this could affect their eligibility.
  • Encouraging patients to continue using their MaineCare benefits to access covered healthcare services, including getting checkups and preventive care and refilling prescriptions, while they remain eligible.
  • Helping reassure patients that an early awareness letter does not mean their coverage has already changed.

Resources:

We developed resources to help providers understand these federal changes and answer patient questions. You can find these resources in this linked toolkit.

MaineCare and OFI will continue to share updates through provider e-messages and our webpage and other typical communication channels as additional information becomes available.

See the Non-citizen Resource Guide for resources that you can share with your patients to help support them in preparing for this change, and after their full MaineCare coverage ends. This list will be continually updated as we become aware of new resources.

If you have additional resources for us to add, please email MaineCare at Communications.MaineCare@maine.gov

If members have questions about covered services, please have them call Member Services at 1-800-977-6740.

Thank you for your continued partnership and for helping to ensure MaineCare members receive accurate information and access to the care they need.

item.title: US Labor Department finds Wisconsin food manufacturer repeatedly exposed workers to safety hazards following 2 incidents, 3 fatalities — U.S. Department of Labor — News Releases
item.description: JANESVILLE, WI – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited a Wisconsin-based food products manufacturer after two incidents involving industrial kettles releasing hot steam and liquid, causing three worker deaths and two serious injuries.Investigators with the department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration responded to the first incident on Feb. 12, 2026, at IPMF LLC, operating as NaturPak. The incident involved the lid of an industrial kettle unexpectedly opening after a clogged vent line led to pressure building up, and then releasing steam, liquid, and organic material onto two employees nearby. One of the employees was also struck by an object and suffered a concussion. Both employees were hospitalized, and one later passed away because of complications from their injuries. A month later, OSHA investigators responded to another incident involving multiple worker hospitalizations on March 18, when a kettle lid opened while under pressure releasing steam, hot liquid, and organic material, burning three workers. Two workers were fatally injured and another hospitalized. OSHA issued the employer one serious citation for the design and usage of kettles leading to pressure and thermal burn hazards; a repeat citation for exposing workers to falls to lower levels; and an other-than-serious citation for failing to notify employees working adjacent to permit-required confined spaces.OSHA also issued serious citations for exposing workers to thermal hazards without quick access to emergency water. The employer also received citations for exposing workers to falls into the kettles and for failure to assess personal protective equipment for thermal risks. In addition, OSHA issued repeat citations for failure to develop, document, and utilize lockout/tagout procedures for the kettles and failure to train employees on lockout/tagout procedures. item.content:encoded:
WHEREAS, in 1996, Governor Angus S. King, Jr. and a unanimous Maine Legislature established the Maine International Trade Center as a public-private partnership, merging existing state trade-development efforts together to support Maine businesses and strengthen Maine’s economy through international commerce; and

WHEREAS, for three decades, the Maine International Trade Center has adapted to sweeping changes in technology, global markets, and trade policy while remaining a trusted, nonpartisan international economic development partner; and

WHEREAS, the Maine International Trade Center has become Maine’s leading source for international business assistance, providing customized consulting, market intelligence, technical assistance, funding, education, and worldwide connections to exporters and importers of every size in all 16 counties; and

WHEREAS, the Maine International Trade Center has worked with thousands of clients and facilitated approximately $350 million in export sales, helping Maine products, services, and innovations reach customers around the world while supporting jobs and economic opportunity in rural, coastal, and urban communities; and

WHEREAS, trade missions led by the Maine International Trade Center have carried Maine businesses from neighboring Canadian provinces to markets across Europe, Asia, Latin America, and beyond, while international delegations and partnerships have brought new relationships, ideas, and opportunities home to Maine; and

WHEREAS, in 2016, the United States Department of Commerce honored the Maine International Trade Center with the President’s “E” Award, the nation’s highest recognition for significant contributions to the expansion of United States exports, and its Future Global Leaders program has provided practical international business experience to more than 200 interns; and

WHEREAS, the Maine International Trade Center’s success reflects the dedication of its staff, board members, business members, public officials, and partners, whose collaboration has ensured that Maine businesses in communities large and small have a place at the international table;

NOW, THEREFORE, be it resolved that I, Janet T. Mills, Governor of the State of Maine, do hereby proclaim August 18, 2026, as the

30TH ANNIVERSARY OF THE MAINE INTERNATIONAL TRADE CENTER

throughout the State of Maine and I encourage all Maine people to join me in recognizing three decades of service by the Maine International Trade Center and celebrating its continued work to connect Maine businesses, people, and communities to the world.

In testimony whereof, I have caused 
the Great Seal of the State to be 
hereunto affixed GIVEN under my 
hand at Augusta this seventeenth day 
of August Two Thousand Twenty-Six

Maine Blood Donation Day

throughout the State of Maine, and I urge all Maine people to support our local blood drives as saving lives and protecting our residents is our primary goal.

Attention Trading Partners: MIHMS Upgrade October Payment Cycle Changes and System Access Limitations

Aug 21, 2026

As previously communicated, the Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) is preparing to launch an upgraded version of MIHMS, MaineCare’s claims processing system. The upgrade is currently scheduled to go live on October 10, 2026. To support a smooth transition, OMS must implement temporary system access limitations and adjustments to payment cycles in October.

From Friday, October 2 at 8:00 PM until Monday, October 12 at 8:00 AM, MIHMS will be in a “data freeze” while OMS completes final system readiness and transition activities.

Changes to October payment cycles:

Review this information and plan billing accordingly to prepare for the transition.

Payment Cycle Date Payment Impact Claim Submission Deadline for Inclusion in Payment Cycle*
Wednesday, 9/30/26 Last regular payment before the data freeze Friday, 9/25/26, 5:00 AM
Thursday, 10/1/26 Extra payment before the data freeze Wednesday, 9/30/26, 5:00 AM
There will be no payment on Wednesday, October 7.
Thursday, 10/15/26 First payment after data freeze, in upgraded system

Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) submission: Continuous through data freeze up to Tuesday, 10/13/26, 2:00 PM

Portal submission:

Before data freeze: Friday, 10/2/26, 7:59 PM

After data freeze: Tuesday, 10/13/26, 2:00 PM
Wednesday, 10/21/26 Regular payment, in upgraded system Friday, 10/16/26, 5:00 AM

*As always, timely submission does not guarantee that the claim will process in time for the next payment cycle. OMS may take up to 30 days to process and pay a claim, depending on any edits or issues that may cause the claim to pend for manual review, as well as other processing requirements that may require the full 30-day timeframe.

Non-claims payments:

By September 1, OMS will communicate with any providers expecting non-claims payments that may be affected by the schedule described above.

Preparing for the changes to October payment cycles:

Beginning September 1, 2026 7:00 AM, OMS will return the HealthPAS Online Portal to its previous regular operating hours. Providers will again have 24/7 access to the portal, for additional flexibility and time to submit claims outside of standard business hours. 

We strongly encourage providers to submit claims approaching timely filing limits in the next few weeks to avoid potential submission delays. The planned data freeze does not modify existing Medicaid timely filing requirements. Providers remain responsible for ensuring claims are submitted within the established timely filing guidelines.

Other system access limitations:

Providers can find other expected impacts of the data freeze in this FAQ. Topics include:

  • HealthPAS Online Portal, including impacts on submitting claims, submitting prior authorizations, and checking member eligibility
  • Provider Enrollment Application (PEA)
  • Value-Based Purchasing Management System (VMS) Portal
  • Paper & fax document submissions
  • Provider Services & Member Services call centers
  • Value Added Network (VAN) Trading Partners
  • Prior authorizations for prescriptions and behavioral health services
  • Electronic Visit Verification (EVV)

You can also check the OMS Provider Resources webpage, in the first box of information called “Health PAS Online Portal,” for the most recent information about the upgrade.

For questions or clarifications, please contact Provider Services at 1-866-690-5585. Please note, Provider Services does not have additional information beyond what is shared in this message and in the FAQ linked above.

2027 MaineCare Eligibility Changes: Information, Resources, and Partner Briefing

Aug 21, 2026

The federal government is making changes to MaineCare (Maine’s Medicaid program). These changes apply to Medicaid programs across the country. Last week the Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) sent out a Save-the-Date for an August 24, 2026, partner and provider briefing on upcoming changes to MaineCare eligibility. There is still time to register!  

The Office for Family Independence (OFI) and OMS are working together to implement these changes as smoothly as possible to avoid disruptions in coverage for eligible Mainers. Our goal is to provide Mainers with clear, accurate, and actionable information so they can confidently understand how these changes may affect them. 

What is changing?  

As of January 1, 2027, the following MaineCare eligibility changes will start:   

For MaineCare Expansion adults:  

  • New Work Requirements; and  

  • Eligibility renewals every 6 months instead of every 12 months.  

For all MaineCare members:  

  • Reductions in retroactive coverage.   

MaineCare Expansion members are adults between 19 and 64 years old who have MaineCare based on their income. They do not meet the Social Security disability guidelines or have Medicare.

What can MaineCare Members Do Now? 

The most important things MaineCare members can do right now are: 

  • Keep their contact information up to date with OFI,  

  • Read any letters they receive, 

  • Continue renewing their coverage as required, and  

  • Continue using their MaineCare benefits. 

We know that members rely on their healthcare providers for trusted information about MaineCare. We appreciate the value that adds, as well as the additional work. Our goal is to support providers through these changes 

Resources to be aware of right now include:  

  • Save the Date: DHHS Partner Briefing on Federal Medicaid Work Requirements and Increased Renewals on August 24, 2026 – register today 

  • Webpages: Federal Changes webpage, MaineCare.gov/FederalChanges, and Work Requirements webpage, MaineCare.gov/Work 

  • Communication tools: A Partner Communications Toolkit for the MaineCare Expansion member changes is available on the Work Requirements webpage. 

  • We are working closely with Maine’s Medicaid Ombudsman program, operated by Consumers for Affordable Health Care, to support community partners who assist Mainers with navigating the MaineCare application and renewal process.  

  • OMS will share a message next week with information about an upcoming pathway for providers to share data with us to support MaineCare eligibility determinations.  

Please note: Maine is still working through key details with the federal government, and we will continue to communicate about who is affected and the steps Expansion members will need to take as we approach 2027.

item.content:encoded:
Hello, this is Governor Janet Mills, and thank you for listening.

You know, we want every person at every stage of their life to be confident they can rent or buy a home that's the right size for their family and for their budget and be able to stay there as long as they want. No one should be afraid that a sudden rent increase will break their budget or that someone will buy the land right out from under them and raise rents.

When Hidden Circle Mobile Home Park in Jay went up for sale, that's exactly what the residents were afraid of: someone hiking up the rent and eventually pushing people out of their homes.

According to the 2024 data, nearly 10 percent of Maine people live in manufactured housing, including mobile home communities. Forty-five thousand people in Maine live in a mobile home park. Out-of-state companies have started buying up some of Maine's mobile home parks and then significantly raising rents, in some cases as high as 50 percent. 

And rent increases don't necessarily mean nicer parks either, no improvements necessarily. Corporations know that residents can't easily pick up their home and move it elsewhere, no matter how much the company neglects the park. As one resident in Jay said, "At one time, the park used to look nice. Now they've stopped that, and yet they have increased our rent. If this continues to have higher lot rent payments, then I'm not going to be able to live where I am."

The buying up of mobile home parks by out-of-state entities is a nationwide trend, but here in Maine, we're doing something about it. Last year, we enacted the "Right of First Refusal" law, which requires that residents of a mobile home park be given a chance to purchase their park if they can put together a matching offer when it's put up for sale. That measure strengthened our 2023 "Opportunity to Purchase" law, which required that residents of a mobile home park be allowed to present a competitive offer to buy their park if it's put up for sale.

Well, earlier this week, I visited Jay to celebrate the first residents to take advantage of our new "Right of First Refusal" law to purchase their park, instead of being left to the whims of an out-of-state buyer. Hidden Circle is now the 14th resident-owned manufactured home community in Maine. Resident-owned—isn't that great?

In addition to financing from the Genesis Fund and Maine Community Foundation, Hidden Circle Mobile Home Community was able to make the $1 million purchase to protect these 31 lots with $310,000 as well from our Mobile Home Park Preservation Fund.

My Administration and the Legislature dedicated $8 million in total in recent years to MaineHousing to create this Mobile Home Park Preservation Fund to assist residents in purchasing their own mobile home parks. With that funding, more than 900 homes are expected to be preserved across six parks from Brunswick to Bangor, Turner to Saco.

Last month, nation-leading laws to further protect mobile home park residents took effect in Maine, including laws to limit rent increases, laws to make it easier to expand mobile home parks, and laws creating a way for mobile homeowners to obtain a mortgage—and that could save them hundreds of dollars every month in housing costs.

I was proud to sign those bills into law earlier this year to protect residents in Jay and other towns across Maine from predatory, out-of-state companies. Now, the residents of Hidden Circle Park in Jay have control over how much rent to charge and how that money will be spent. They have control over their common infrastructure, and they can make improvements as they see fit.

Well, we still have a lot more work to do to protect Maine people and mobile home parks from being exploited by companies who simply want to use them to extract a profit, but I am proud of how we worked together with the Legislature to preserve this vital form of housing for people in Maine.

This is Governor Janet Mills, and thank you for listening.

The Employment Situation in Maine - July 2026

The 3.1 unemployment rate was unchanged for the fourth consecutive month. Nonfarm wage and salary jobs have remained within a narrow range for 27 consecutive months.

Seasonally Adjusted Statewide Labor Force Estimates

The unemployment rate remained at 3.1 percent in July. Unemployment rates have remained within a narrow range between 3.1 and 3.3 percent for 23 consecutive months. Unemployment has been below four percent for 55 months, the longest duration on record. Maine's unemployment rate has been below the U.S. average for more than 18 years, and remains below the long-term average of 5.4 percent for the state since 1976. Unemployment averaged 4.2 percent for New England and 4.1 percent for the U.S. in the month.

The labor force participation rate averaged 59 percent in the last three months, modestly lower than the three months through April. The employment-to-population ratio was also modestly lower in the three months through July compared to the three months prior.

Seasonally Adjusted Statewide Nonfarm Jobs Estimates

Preliminary seasonally adjusted estimates indicate that in July, nonfarm wage and salary jobs were little changed from June. Most sectors exhibited little net job change over-the-month.

Job estimates have stayed within a narrow range near 660,000 for 27 consecutive months (estimates ranging less than one half of one percent higher or lower each month). Over the last year, a decrease in jobs in the professional and business services sector and smaller decreases in other sectors were mostly offset by increases that were also spread across several sectors.

These estimates are derived from two monthly surveys. The Current Population Survey collects information from households on labor force status, including labor force participation, employment, and unemployment. The Current Employment Statistics survey collects information from nonfarm employers by industry on the number of wage and salary jobs, hours worked, and wages paid to individuals on their payrolls. Both surveys are administered by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. Preliminary estimates from the two surveys sometimes diverge in direction or magnitude of change. Over extended periods they tend to be more aligned. Maine's Fall Foliage Season Set to Begin with Weekly Reports, New Event Feature

August 24, 2026

First 2026 foliage report arrives September 9; communities and organizations invited to share fall events with foliage visitors

Augusta, MAINE - One of Maine's most anticipated seasons is just around the corner, bringing brilliant color, harvest traditions, and countless reasons to explore the state.

The Maine Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry (DACF) will launch its 2026 fall foliage reporting season on Wednesday, September 9, at MaineFoliage.com and by email to subscribers. Reports will be issued each Wednesday throughout the season, tracking the progression of fall color from northern Maine and higher elevations southward toward the coast.

This year, DACF is adding another way to help residents and visitors experience fall in Maine: organizations, communities, and event organizers are invited to submit fall events for consideration for inclusion in the weekly foliage reports.

"Fall foliage is more than something to see, it's an invitation to experience Maine," said DACF Commissioner Amanda Beal. "Whether that means visiting a farm, hiking a trail, attending a harvest festival, exploring a downtown, or simply following a scenic by-way, our weekly reports help people follow the color and discover more of Maine along the way."

2026 Fall Foliage Season Preview

DACF Maine Forest Service experts expect peak fall foliage to develop along its typical progression from north to south, with trees at higher elevations generally developing color before those at lower elevations.

Maine's tremendous diversity of tree species, landscapes, and growing conditions helps create both its spectacular fall color and an extended viewing season. Northern and coastal areas offer striking contrasts between evergreens and colorful maples, birches, and oaks, while inland forests provide a broad palette of fall color set among Maine's abundant lakes, rivers, mountains, and working landscapes.

While foliage conditions can vary from one location to another, Maine's healthy and diverse forests continue to provide outstanding opportunities for fall color.

"The great thing about fall foliage in Maine is that there isn't just one place or one moment to experience it," said MFS Director and State Forester Patty Cormier. "Color develops at different times across the state and across different landscapes. If conditions aren't at their best in one location, spectacular foliage is often just down the road."

Fall color develops through a combination of shorter daylight, cooler temperatures, leaf pigments, moisture, and other environmental conditions. As days shorten, trees slow their production of chlorophyll, revealing the yellow and orange pigments already present in leaves. Cooler temperatures and other environmental factors can also influence the red and purple colors associated with anthocyanin pigments.

Because Maine's forests contain such a diverse mix of tree species and growing conditions, the result is a constantly changing mosaic of color throughout the season.

New: Share Your Fall Event with Maine Foliage Visitors

For 2026, DACF is inviting organizations, communities, farms, nonprofits, municipalities, and event organizers to submit public fall events for possible inclusion in Maine's Weekly Foliage Reports. DACF is looking for more activities that give residents and visitors another reason to get out and experience autumn in Maine, including:

  • Harvest festivals and agricultural fairs
  • Farm and food events
  • Outdoor recreation and nature-based activities
  • Arts and cultural events
  • Community festivals and celebrations
  • Other public events that complement the fall foliage experience

Events should take place during Maine's fall foliage reporting season, generally mid-September through mid-October, and must be open to the public.

SUBMIT YOUR FALL EVENT

DACF will review events based on timing, location, relevance to the foliage season, and available space. Submitted information may be edited for length, clarity, and style.

Follow the Color at MaineFoliage.com

Throughout the season, MaineFoliage.com is the official resource for tracking Maine's changing fall color. Weekly reports provide foliage conditions across the state and help residents and visitors decide when and where to explore. The first report will be published on Wednesday, September 9, 2026, with updated reports following every Wednesday through the foliage season.

From Maine's northern forests and western mountains to its lakes, farms, downtowns, and coast, there is no single way to experience fall in Maine. Following the changing color and exploring the places, people, events, and landscapes along the way is part of what makes the season special.

About Maine's Fall Foliage Reports

For 68 years, the DACF has produced Maine's official fall foliage reports, drawing on observations from forestry and conservation professionals across the state. Published weekly throughout the season, the reports track the progression of color and leaf drop across seven foliage zones and provide information and resources to help residents and visitors make the most of Maine's spectacular fall season.

Aug 24, 2026

The upgrade will include a new “MaineCare Partner Portal” that will replace what is known today as the “Health PAS Online Portal.” Please note that, until the October go-live, we will continue using the name “Health PAS Online Portal” in communications related to current functionality. 

You can read more about the benefits to providers and members on the Health PAS Online Portal. 

Trading Partners Preparation 

This is the final notice reminding trading partners to take action to prepare for the transition to the upgraded online portal, called the MaineCare Partner Portal. 

Trading partners include providers, billing agents, health plans, clearinghouses, and business associates. Trading partners have an important role to play in supporting a smooth transition and uninterrupted access to the portal after go-live. 

Portal Access Impacts and Required Actions Before Go‑Live 

The preparation activities and changes below will improve system security by ensuring the right people have the right access, at go-live and ongoing. Most actions are only for Admin (R7) users.  

Most important: Providers with duplicate emails need to make changes to their portal user accounts now to assist with account migration to the upgraded portal. On September 1, we will terminate current Admin (R7) user accounts that share an email address with another user account. We will not terminate Admin (R7) user accounts if they are the only Admin (R7) on the Trading Partner account. 

If a user account is terminated and they still need portal access, another user with Admin Rights (R7) can invite the terminated user using a unique email address, not the one previously used.

Your Action 

Why it Matters 

What’s Next? 

At go-live, MaineCare will only migrate Admin (R7) accounts to the new portal. 

  

MaineCare will not migrate inactive accounts. 

Designate at least one active Admin (R7) per organization, and two for backup coverage. 

  

Trading Partners with large user populations should plan for sufficient Admin (R7) coverage to avoid access delays after go-live; we recommend one Admin (R7) per 25 users. 

  

Remove inactive Admin (R7) accounts.

Trading Partners have an existing and ongoing responsibility to remove inactive users to help keep our systems and data secure. 

  

We will monitor the number and activity of Admin (R7) users per Trading Partner and will reach out to individual Trading Partners if needed. 

In the new portal, your username will be your email address. 

MaineCare will not migrate accounts that share an email address. 

Confirm that each active Admin (R7) user account has its own unique email address. 

OMS will deactivate accounts that continue to share email addresses as we approach go-live. 

After go-live, Admin (R7) users will need immediate access to the portal to invite other users and avoid disruption in Trading Partner work. 

We will monitor accounts that share email addresses and will reach out to individual Trading Partners if needed. 

Admin (R7) users will invite other users to the portal and designate your roles after go-live.

  • Know who needs a user account in the new portal 

  • Know the permission level each user will need to have 

  

Admin (R7) users will need to invite other users shortly after go-live to avoid a disruption in Trading Partner work.

Minors were also permitted to operate a commercial-grade batter mixer, which is prohibited for workers under age 18, violating federal child labor provisions under the FLSA. The employer also permitted 14- and 15-year-olds to work outside of legally allowed hours.The franchisee paid $62,235 in civil money penalties to resolve the child labor violations and signed an enhanced compliance agreement that affects all seven of its current and future locations. Under the agreement, the employer will modify the uniforms of employees under 16-years-old to distinguish them from older employees, ensure youth workers are informed of their rights, and hold managers accountable to child labor regulations, including the possibility of termination for violations. In fiscal year 2025, the department investigated 976 cases with child labor violations involving 5,272 minors nationwide, including 773 minors employed in violation of hazardous occupation standards. The department assessed employers more than $37 million in civil money penalties to address violations.Employees and employers can contact the Wage and Hour Division with questions and requests for compliance assistance at its toll-free helpline, 866-4US-WAGE (487-9243). Employers are encouraged to use the agency’s industry-specific compliance assistance toolkits to learn about their responsibilities under the laws enforced by the division. Learn more about the Wage and Hour Division, including youth employment regulations on dangerous jobs that are prohibited for workers under age 18.

item.description: NEW ORLEANS – The U.S. Department of Labor has recovered $101,125 in back wages from three Baton Rouge area Japanese restaurants after a federal investigation found federal minimum wage and overtime violations. WHEREAS, on August 24, 2016, the eve of the National Park Service’s 100th anniversary, President Barack Obama officially designated 87,500 acres of Maine’s North Woods as the Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument; and

WHEREAS, for thousands of years, this land has been home to Wabanaki people who traversed the Penobscot’s waterways and negotiated the deep woods in search of food, furs, medicines and other resources; and

WHEREAS, countless others have come to know the beauty and serenity of this land that native peoples had already known for centuries – those like Henry David Thoreau, Theodore Roosevelt and Percival Baxter – who helped share this special place with the world and commanded us to preserve it; and 

WHEREAS, this land has also been vital to generations of Maine people who make their living by logging and working in the forest products industry; and 

WHEREAS, the establishment of the monument would not have been possible without the lifelong dedication of Roxanne Quimby and her family to preserve this precious piece of Maine, along with the conservationists, philanthropists, and advocates who continue supporting it, including the Friends of Katahdin Woods & Waters; and

WHEREAS, since its creation, the monument has greatly benefited neighboring communities as visitors from in and out of Maine travel to experience its beauty, and in 2024 alone, visitors spent $2.7 million in local communities near the park; and

WHEREAS, with the Katahdin Woods and Waters Monument, we have safeguarded this place that has meant so much to so many people, ensuring that everyone can come camp, hike, fish, take in a night sky, or just enjoy nature in its purest form for generations to come;

NOW THEREFORE, be it resolved that I, Janet T. Mills, Governor of the State of Maine, do hereby proclaim August 24, 2026 as the 

10th Anniversary of the Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument

and I urge everyone to visit the monument, embrace the raw beauty of Maine, and do their part in protecting and preserving our natural environment. 

In testimony whereof, I have caused 
the Great Seal of the State to be 
hereunto affixed GIVEN under my 
hand at Augusta this twentieth day 
of August Two Thousand Twenty-Six

Attention Trading Partners: Training for New MaineCare Partner Portal

Aug 25, 2026

We have previously shared that a refreshed and upgraded MIHMS, with a new “MaineCare Partner Portal,” is coming in October 2026. This will replace the current HealthPAS Online Portal. We are now inviting trading partners to register for training starting September 8, 2026 to help you prepare for the transition to the new portal. Trading partners include providers, billing agents, health plans, clearinghouses, and business associates. Trading partners have an important role to play in supporting a smooth transition and uninterrupted access to the portal after go-live.

Gainwell Technologies will be leading live virtual instructor-led training sessions. These courses will provide the knowledge and skills needed to navigate the new portal, complete daily business functions, and use new portal features. Training demonstrations, materials, and supporting resources will help participants prepare for a successful transition.

Steps you need to take to attend training

  • Review the available training topics listed below and identify the sessions that align with your role and responsibilities.
  • Use the LMS registration (instructions below) to create an account, access the training catalog, and enroll in applicable sessions.
  • Contact Gainwell (instructions below) if you need assistance.
  • Recorded sessions and other training materials will be available in the LMS after training sessions for ongoing reference.

MaineCare Partner Portal Training Sessions

Course Name

Description

ME - TPT - Migrated Trading Partner Log In and Account Maintenance Training (ILC)

Learn how to complete first-time login activities, configure multi-factor authentication (MFA), manage user accounts and permissions, perform account maintenance activities, and understand electronic data interchange (EDI) certification requirements and status monitoring. This course is only for Admin (R7) users.

ME - TPT - Trading Partner Registration and Account Maintenance Training (ILC)

Learn how to register a new Trading Partner account, complete account activation, manage users and permissions, associate providers and billing agents, navigate the portal, and maintain account information.

ME - TPT - Authorization, Referrals and Certifications Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit and manage authorizations, process referrals, monitor certification requests and statuses, and access related portal functionality.

ME - TPT - Dental Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit dental claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions.

ME - TPT - Institutional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit institutional claims, monitor claim processing and status, and navigate claim-related portal functions.

ME - TPT - Professional Claim Entry & Claim Management Training (ILC)

Learn how to submit professional claims, monitor claim status, review payment information, access remittance advice, and complete related claim activities.

ME - TPT - MaineCare Partner Public Portal Training (ILC)

Learn about publicly available portal functionality, portal resources and reference materials, secure messaging, Trading Partner tools, and available resources.

 

LMS Access and Course Registration Instructions

Use the following steps to register for MaineCare Partner Portal training. Multiple sessions are available for each course to allow for scheduling flexibility.

  1. Go to the LMS registration site: https://mmislearningcenter.myabsorb.com/#/login.
  2. Sign in using your existing account or click Sign Up on the right side of the window to create a new account.
  3. If you need a new account, enter the enrollment key: De8pO9CBYXYB-aOCY8qp on the Sign Up window.
  4. Complete the required registration information to create your account. Note: You can enter your workplace address.
  5. The Learner Dashboard appears. From this window, you can access previous trainings, search for and enroll in the appropriate training sessions, and review your transcript.
  6. To locate the appropriate courses, search using “TPT” or the course name from the table above in the search bar at the top of the window or by opening the Course Catalog tile.
  7. Click Choose Session for each course you need to complete, then enroll in the session that best fits your schedule.
  8. You will receive an email confirmation regarding the success of your enrollment. Additionally, you will receive a Microsoft Teams calendar event for each session.
  9. On the day of the training, access the training via one of the following methods:
    • Access the Teams Meeting hyperlink from the course confirmation email.
    • Click the Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink within the Outlook/Teams calendar event.
    • Access My Courses in the LMS and click the appropriate Microsoft Teams meeting hyperlink.

Do not forward meeting invitations to other attendees. Each participant must register through the LMS to receive course acces

item.description: Maine Human Rights Commission # 51 State House Station, Augusta, ME 04333-0051 Physical location: 19 Union Street, Augusta, ME 04330 ■ ■Phone (207) 624-6290 Fax (207) 624-8729 TTY: Maine Relay 711 www.maine.gov/mhrc Kit Thomson Crossman Barbara Archer Hirsch EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR COMMISSION COUNSEL MAINE HUMAN RIGHTS COMMISSION Public Guidance Statement RE: HUD's New Emotional Support Animal Enforcement Guidance and Maine Housing Providers' Continuing Obligations Under the Maine Human Rights Act August 4, 2026 What Has Changed at the Federal Level On May 22, 2026, the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) issued an enforcement memorandum announcing that it will no longer find reasonable cause in housing complaints involving emotional support animals (ESAs). In other words, animals that provide comfort, companionship, or otherwise mitigate the effects of a person’s disability but have not been individually trained to perform specific disability-related tasks are no longer protected at the federal level. Going forward, HUD will pursue enforcement only where an animal has been trained to perform work or tasks directly related to a person's disability (essentially, HUD has imported the Americans with Disabilities Act's narrower "service animal" definition into Fair Housing Act enforcement). HUD simultaneously rescinded its 2020 guidance, which had for years provided meaningful protections to individuals who rely on ESAs as part of their disability-related care. After 35 years without updating its regulations in this area, the federal government's chosen solution has been, perhaps unsurprisingly, to reduce protections rather than clarify them. The Maine Human Rights Commission takes note of this development. We also take note that it changes nothing in Maine. Bradbury Mountain State Park Selected as 2026 Leave No Trace Spotlight; Community Events Set for September 3-5

August 26, 2026

Three days of activities will bring together Leave No Trace, Maine State Parks, volunteers, and community partners to celebrate and care for one of Maine's treasured outdoor spaces.

Pownal - The Maine Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry (DACF) announced today that Bradbury Mountain State Park in Pownal has been selected as a 2026 Leave No Trace Spotlight, bringing three days of community events, outdoor education, and hands-on stewardship to the park and surrounding area September 3-5, 2026.

"Bradbury Mountain is a place people return to again and again, to hike, bike, gather with family, take in the view, and enjoy being outside," said Chris Silsbee, Manager of Bradbury Mountain State Park. Being selected as a Leave No Trace Spotlight gives us a great opportunity to bring the community together, have some fun, and put stewardship into action. Whether you join us for trivia, sit around the campfire, or spend Saturday working on a trail, there's a way for everyone to be part of it.

Activities begin Thursday evening in Freeport and continue through Saturday at Bradbury Mountain State Park.

  • September 3, 2026: Leave No Trace Trivia Night
  • September 4, 2026: Fireside with the Ranger, Leave No Trace Staff & Hot Dog Roast
  • September 4, 2026: Leave No Trace Outreach Tent
  • September 5, 2026: Leave No Trace Event & Stewardship Project
  • September 5, 2026: Leave No Trace Stewardship Project

There is also a special incentive for early arrivals: the first 25 cars through the park gate whose driver says, "Bigfoot Leaves No Trace at Bradbury," will receive a gift bag featuring items from local event sponsors.

About the Leave No Trace Spotlight Program

Each year, Leave No Trace selects nominated outdoor areas for its Spotlight program, which brings communities together to care for and protect places people love to visit. Spotlights combine education, community outreach, and hands-on stewardship to help address impacts from outdoor recreation while giving visitors practical tools they can use long after the event ends. Bradbury Mountain State Park's Spotlight is supported by the Subaru/Leave No Trace Traveling Team, Maine State Parks, community volunteers, and local partners.

About Bradbury Mountain State Park

Bradbury Mountain State Park, located in Pownal, is one of Maine's original five state parks. The park offers more than 20 miles of trails for hiking, mountain biking, and horseback riding, along with camping and opportunities to experience the area's natural and cultural history. The summit of Bradbury Mountain provides expansive views and is a popular location for observing the annual migration of hawks and other birds of prey. For information about Bradbury Mountain State Park, visit the Maine State Parks website.

Notice of Agency Rulemaking Proposal

 

Agency: Department of Health and Human Services, Office of MaineCare Services, Division of Policy

Chapter Number and Rule Title: 10-144 C.M.R. Ch. 101, MaineCare Benefits Manual (MBM) Ch. II, Sec. 20, Home and Community Based Services for Adults with Other Related Conditions

Type of Rule: Routine Technical

Brief Summary: This Section 20 rule regulates home and community-based services (HCBS) that are authorized by a federal Medicaid Section 1915(c) HCBS waiver that meets federal standards. MBM Ch. II, Sec. 20 authorizes MaineCare HCBS waiver services for adults with conditions other than autism spectrum disorder that are related to but distinguishable from intellectual disabilities. Through this rulemaking the Department proposes to: align similar processes, new services, service descriptions, definitions, and provider requirements with Maine’s four other Section 1915(c) waivers; make permanent certain flexibilities first utilized for Section 20 services during the Covid-19 Public Health Emergency (PHE); strengthen safeguards for Members by enacting the Plan of Corrective Action and Request for Exceptions processes; and incorporate the Department’s Global HCBS Rule (MBM Ch. I, Sec. 6) by reference.

Additionally, the Department proposes to require ` Section 20 providers to comply with 10-149 C.M.R. ch. 1, sec. 2-Grievances once this new grievance rule is adopted pursuant to the Maine Administrative Procedure Act (APA). The Department is concurrently undertaking major substantive rulemaking under the APA for MBM Ch. III, Sec. 20, to establish reimbursement procedures for the new and updated services described in this rulemaking. Please see accompanying draft rule for a complete list of all proposed changes in this agency’s rulemaking. See http://www.maine.gov/dhhs/oms/rules/index.shtml for rules and related rulemaking documents.

CHAPTER NUMBER AND RULE TITLE: 10-144 C.M.R. Ch. 101, MaineCare Benefits Manual (MBM), Ch. III, Sec. 20, Allowances for Home and Community-Based Services for Adults with Other Related Conditions

TYPE OF RULE: Major Substantive

BRIEF SUMMARY: Section 20 in the MBM authorizes home and community-based services (HCBS) under a CMS-approved Section 1915(c) waiver. The Department proposes to amend the Chapter III, Section 20 rule to establish the reimbursement methodology for new services being added under a companion, Chapter II, Section 20 rule, and to remove rates of reimbursement for all services which will now be listed in Rate Schedules on the Department’s website pursuant to 22 M.R.S. § 3177-J. Such cost-of-living adjustments will satisfy the requirements for direct support worker wages set forth in 22 M.R.S. § 7402(1).

See http://www.maine.gov/dhhs/oms/rules/index.shtml for rules and related rulemaking documents.

Once adopted, the proposed Chapter III, Section 20 rule will only be provisional: as a major substantive rule, Chapter III, Section 20 requires Legislative approval before it can be legally effective. item.title: Trump Administration issues guidance on health-contingent wellness programs, including tobacco cessation programs — U.S. Department of Labor — News Releases
item.description: WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of Labor announced today that its Employee Benefits Security Administration, along with the departments of Health and Human Services and Treasury, issued guidance related to questions raised in dozens of class-action lawsuits challenging the tobacco surcharges some employers add to premiums for their group health plans through workplace wellness programs. The Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996 and the Affordable Care Act allow employers to reward employees for healthy habits through wellness programs. Wellness programs can cover things like nutrition, weight loss, tobacco cessation, fitness, alcohol and drug abuse assistance, managing stress, or general health education.The FAQs released today announce the departments’ approach to enforcement for health-contingent wellness programs, which are programs that reward an employee if they satisfy a standard related to a health factor. Until further guidance or regulations are issued, the departments will not take enforcement action against plans or issuers that do not give employees the wellness program reward retroactively to the beginning of the plan year after the employee completes a reasonable alternative standard. item.description: WATSONTOWN, PA – The U.S. Department of Labor has cited a brick manufacturer with three willful and four serious violations for knowingly exposing its workers to unsafe levels of respirable silica dust at its Watsontown plant.On Feb. 12, 2026, investigators with the department’s Occupational Safety and Health Administration inspected General Shale Brick Inc. – doing business as Watsontown Brick Company – as part of the agency’s Site‑Specific Targeting inspection plan and national emphasis program on silica as well as a review of the company’s injury and illness records. OSHA found that workers in Plant 3, where molded brick is made, breathed in silica dust above safe limits. A past violation for missing respirator fit tests, at the company’s Augusta, Georgia site, led to an added repeat violation.OSHA issued three willful, four serious, one repeat, and one other-than-serious violation, with proposed penalties of $496,528.The company has 15 business days from receipt of its citations to comply, request an informal conference with OSHA’s area director, or contest the findings before the independent Occupational Safety and Health Review Commission. Maine DEP Initiates Legal Action Against Mallinckrodt US LLC to Address Cleanup Failures at Orrington Site

Maine Department of Environmental Protection sent this bulletin at 08/25/2026 03:45 PM EDT

--- PRESS RELEASE ---

For Immediate Release

 

Maine DEP Initiates Legal Action Against Mallinckrodt US LLC to Address Cleanup Failures at Orrington Site

 

AUGUSTA, August 25, 2026 — The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) filed a formal complaint today in Penobscot County Superior Court against Mallinckrodt US LLC (Mallinckrodt). The complaint details the failure by Mallinckrodt to complete cleanup of the former Holtrachem site located along the Penobscot River in Orrington, Maine, one of Maine’s most contaminated sites. Mallinckrodt has not met the remediation standards required in the DEP’s 2008 Designation of Uncontrolled Hazardous Substance Site and Order, that was affirmed in 2010 by the Board of Environmental Protection (BEP) in its own slightly modified order, affirmed in 2012 by the Maine Business and Consumer Docket, and finally affirmed in 2014 by the Maine Supreme Judicial Court sitting as the Law Court.

The former Holtrachem site was a chloralkali manufacturing facility, which made chemicals commonly used in the pulp and paper industry. Historic operations resulted in a significant amount of contamination, including highly toxic mercury and chloropicrin, in surrounding soils, groundwaters, and the Penobscot River. Site-specific standards were established by the DEP and BEP Orders to ensure that the site would be cleaned up in a manner that would protect public health, safety, and the environment.  Despite these Orders, large areas of soils still remain on site that exceed the site-specific cleanup standards.

The DEP has worked diligently to provide oversight during cleanup of the former Holtrachem site to ensure that Mallinckrodt conducts remediation in compliance with the DEP and BEP Orders. While progress has been made, it began to slow down as early as 2018 when Mallinckrodt began the first of several attempts to seek relief from meeting the Orders’ requirements. Since 2023, Mallinckrodt has ceased any meaningful progress toward remediation at the site.

Prior to today’s filing, two Notices of Violation (NOVs) were issued to Mallinckrodt on March 19, 2025, and October 22, 2025. These NOVs provide more detailed information about Mallinckrodt’s failure to comply with the DEP and BEP Orders. Copies of these NOVs are available on the DEP Mallinckrodt webpage.

The Department is seeking injunctive relief from the Penobscot Superior Court and civil penalties for ongoing violations.

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Contact: Danna Hayes, Danna.hayes@maine.gov

Attorney General Aaron M. Frey Sues United States Postal Service Over Unlawful Attempt to Interfere with States’ Vote-by-Mail Procedures

Lawsuit Seeks to Block Unconstitutional USPS Rule that Directs States to Overhaul Vote-by-Mail Procedures on an Impossible Timeline and Risks Disenfranchising Eligible Voters

AUGUSTA – Attorney General Aaron M. Frey today joined a coalition of 25 states in filing a lawsuit against the United States Postal Service (USPS) challenging its new rule that purports to grant USPS the authority to regulate mail voting in elections.

Tens of millions of voters across the country rely on mail-in ballots, and the coalition argues USPS’s rule will prevent states from effectively administering their mail voting programs, putting voters at risk of being disenfranchised.

“USPS and the President are inflicting violence on free and fair elections through this unlawful attempt to control voting by mail, said Attorney General Frey. “This is not hard: the Constitution does not trust the Executive Branch with the responsibility of facilitating elections and this new rule – this election interference – must be stopped.”

On March 31, President Trump issued an Executive Order attempting to establish a national list of eligible voters and directing the U.S. Postal Service to transmit mail ballots only to voters on the list. On August 21, USPS announced a new rule implementing the President’s demands that require states to register every voter who is eligible to vote by mail with USPS and tasking USPS with compiling the registered voters into state-specific lists. The rule also establishes new design requirements for the mail-in ballot envelopes created by states, which states are required to meet and get approved by USPS. Under the rule, USPS will not deliver ballots to voters who do not appear on the USPS-generated lists and will not deliver ballots in envelopes that fail to comply with the rule’s new standards.

Attorney General Frey and the coalition argue the rule inflicts significant, irreparable harm on states by imposing burdensome mail voting requirements that risk disenfranchising eligible voters. With the start of the general election season mere weeks away, states must bear the cost of redesigning their mail ballot envelopes and securing USPS review and approval before they can even register mail voters with USPS. Within a matter of weeks and without any additional resources, state election officials must also develop new systems to communicate mail voter lists to USPS to ensure that every eligible voter who is entitled to a mail ballot receives one. States must also create new guidance for election officials, train them on the new procedures, and educate the public about the changes prior to the upcoming election.

Even if states were to meet these enormous administrative and financial burdens, the rule could still result in eligible voters not receiving their ballots due to, for instance, administrative errors or flaws in the rushed and untested new procedures.

Over the past several decades, voting by mail has become more popular across the country. In the 2024 general election, 26% of overall votes were cast by mail. Since the inception of vote-by-mail, Congress has never exercised its authority to limit it, and in fact, has only taken action to expand and protect mail voting for military and overseas voters. Congress has also never authorized USPS to monitor or control the transmission of mail ballots.

The coalition argues that USPS’s rule violates the Constitution, which makes clear that states have the primary authority to administer elections, and upends successful, longstanding vote-by-mail procedures. The lawsuit argues the rule is inconsistent with USPS’s governing statutes, ignores USPS’s procedural requirements, violates the Privacy Act, and is inconsistent with federal voting rights law. The coalition asks the court to strike down the unlawful rule and issue a temporary restraining order preventing the rule from taking effect while the litigation proceeds.

This USPS rule is the latest attempt by President Trump to exert federal control over elections and seize states’ constitutional authority to administer elections. In April, Attorney General Frey joined a coalition of 24 states in suing the Trump Administration to block its unlawful Executive Order that prompted the creation of USPS’s rule.

Joining Attorney General Frey in filing this lawsuit, which was co-led by the attorneys general of California, Massachusetts, Nevada, and Washington, are the attorneys general of Arizona, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, District of Columbia, Hawaiʻi, Illinois, Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, North Carolina, Oregon, Rhode Island, Vermont, Virginia, Wisconsin, and the Governor of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.

item.content:encoded:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Contact: Danna Hayes, Danna.hayes@maine.gov

Attorney General Aaron M. Frey Announces Largest Big Tech Settlement in History

Meta to Pay Up to $17 Billion and Implement Sweeping Child-Safety Reforms on Instagram and Facebook

AUGUSTA – Today, Attorney General Aaron M. Frey announced a landmark $17.1 billion multistate settlement with Meta Platforms, Inc.— the largest state consumer protection settlement in history outside the Big Tobacco settlements of the 1990s. The settlement is subject to court approval. In addition to the payment, Meta must implement a sweeping set of safety features designed to protect children on Instagram and Facebook. The agreement resolves claims by 47 States and D.C., Puerto Rico, American Samoa, and the Northern Mariana Islands that the company designed Instagram with addictive features, knowingly exposed young users to serious mental harms, and intentionally misled the public about the safety of its platforms, among other things. This settlement is a victory for the protection of America’s children and an important first step to transform how the entire social media industry designs products for kids and teens. Under the settlement, Maine will receive no less than $56 million.

“This hard-fought settlement provides important protections for children on Meta’s platforms, Instagram and Facebook, and empowers parents with tools to help address the negative impacts of social media use on children,” said Attorney General Frey. “Notably, Meta is agreeing to measures designed to ensure that children under 13 are not on its platforms. While this settlement is an important step, the need to make social media safer for children must extend to the entire industry. We will continue to work with our multistate partners to push for comprehensive changes that prioritize the safety and welfare of children over profit.”

The settlement requires Meta to implement a series of safety features on Instagram and Facebook, including:

  • Daily time limits and “Productive Pauses” for children for most content: for its two platforms, Instagram and Facebook, a combined two-hour daily time limit with mandatory pauses after 15 minutes of continuous use and again at 60 and 90 minutes to interrupt endless scrolling. These limits remain in effect for five years. If Snapchat, TikTok, and YouTube adopt comparable terms, the daily limit on each platform will drop to 60 minutes for 10 years.
  • “Nighttime blocks” restricting children’s access from 12:00 a.m. to 6:00 a.m.
  • Eliminating push notifications during school hours (weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.).
  • Age assurance measures to more effectively verify the age of young users.
  • Safer, age-appropriate content controls, including stronger safeguards against bullying, content promoting eating disorders, and content related to suicide and self-harm.
  • Stronger, more user-friendly parental controls.
  • Limits on social comparison features, including beauty filters and visible “like” counts, that have been linked to poor mental health outcomes in kids and teens.
  • Both the implementation and efficacy of the features will be regularly assessed by an independent auditor and the settling states.

These are critical changes to Instagram and Facebook and more comprehensive than previously ordered by any court.

Beginning in 2021, nearly every attorney general in the country cooperated to investigate the social media industry for designing and promoting platforms to children and teens despite known harms. After a bipartisan, nationwide investigation found that Meta designed Instagram’s features to addict children while internally documenting the resulting mental health harms and failing to warn parents, attorneys general across the country sued Meta individually or as part of a consolidated federal lawsuit. This settlement resolves those cases and claims by the other settling states and territories. The settlement also resolves the states’ claims against Meta for its sharing of nonpublic information about Facebook users with third parties, like Cambridge Analytica, leading up to the 2016 election.

The attorneys general of Alabama, Alaska, American Samoa, Arizona, Arkansas, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, District of Columbia, Georgia, Hawaii, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, Montana, Nebraska, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Northern Mariana Islands, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Puerto Rico, Rhode Island, South Carolina, South Dakota, Tennessee, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, Washington, West Virginia, Wisconsin, and Wyoming joined the settlement.

WHEREAS, honey bees (Apis Mellifera) and other native insects are essential pollinators that contribute to food security by pollinating the plants we use and one-third of the food we consume; and

WHEREAS, honey bees face serious threats from many sources including pests and viruses, loss of habitat, toxic pesticide and herbicide usage, and changes in climate and resulting water patterns; and

WHEREAS, honey bees are essential in the production of Maine's heritage crops including blueberries and apples; and

WHEREAS, Maine's honey bees produce approximately 450,000 pounds of honey each year and contribute an estimated annual $100-150 million to the state’s economy; and

WHEREAS, Maine has almost 2,000 beekeepers ranging from hobbyists with as few as one hive, to part time business owners, to full time commercial beekeepers with thousands of hives; and

WHEREAS, while traditional beekeeping occurred in rural areas of Maine for the purpose of helping pollinate farm crops, beekeeping is now growing in urban areas as the result of rising numbers of hobby beekeepers interested in increasing biodiversity and local food production; and

WHEREAS, the State of Maine has an exemplary apiary inspection program for the protection of honey bees and education of beekeepers in the prevention and spread of apiary diseases and pests; and

WHEREAS, since 1975 the Honey Bee has been recognized as Maine's official state insect; and

WHEREAS, the Maine State Beekeepers Association is celebrating its 50th year of incorporation in 2026, and will host the annual “Bee Fest” on September 13 at the Viles Arboretum in Augusta;

NOW THEREFORE, be it resolved, that I, Janet T. Mills, Governor of the State of Maine do hereby proclaim September 13, 2026 as 

Maine Honey Bee Day

and I encourage all Maine people to join in recognizing the importance of honey bees to our state.

item.description: AUGUSTA, MAINE – A federal judge in Boston blocked the Trump administration from interfering with states’ rights to conduct mail-in voting for the upcoming November elections, now 67 days away. Judge Indira Talwani ruled yesterday that the plaintiffs were likely to succeed in proving the administration’s order was unconstitutional. “Last night’s decision was wonderful news for Maine voters who rely on absentee voting,” Secretary Bellows said . “The judge made clear that the states, not the federal government, are in charge of elections. We will continue to stand with other states and voting rights advocates across the nation to defend the voting rights – including the right to vote by mail – for every citizen.” In the decision, Judge Talwani wrote, “the Constitution charges the States with election administration” going on to say that no law has been passed by Congress that “would permit the USPS to regulate election mail.” The judge went even further to note that with just two months to the election, it would an expensive and likely impossible task for the 2026 election, saying, “Plaintiff States face irreparable harm where they are required to comply with a likely unconstitutional regulation for which compliance is practically impossible.” ### Attachment: read the 08-27-26 order
item.content:encoded:
AUGUSTA, MAINE – A federal judge in Boston blocked the Trump administration from interfering with states’ rights to conduct mail-in voting for the upcoming November elections, now 67 days away. Judge Indira Talwani ruled yesterday that the plaintiffs were likely to succeed in proving the administration’s order was unconstitutional. 

“Last night’s decision was wonderful news for Maine voters who rely on absentee voting,” Secretary Bellows said. “The judge made clear that the states, not the federal government, are in charge of elections. That goes to the heart of our legal fights in court against the Trump Administration. We will continue to stand with other states and voting rights advocates across the nation to defend the voting rights – including the right to vote by mail – for every citizen.”

In the decision, Judge Talwani wrote, “the Constitution charges the States with election administration” going on to say that no law has been passed by Congress that “would permit the USPS to regulate election mail.” The judge went even further to note that with just two months to the election, it would an expensive and likely impossible task for the 2026 election, saying, “Plaintiff States face irreparable harm where they are required to comply with a likely unconstitutional regulation for which compliance is practically impossible.”

item.content:encoded:
WHEREAS, Maine has a rich and storied tradition of hunting and angling that dates back further than the state itself and carries forward to this day; and


WHEREAS, hunting and angling continue to be an integral component of the cultural fabric of communities throughout the state, and over recent years have offered a growing number of participants an opportunity to connect with nature on a personal level while simultaneously providing food security, a sense of self-sufficiency, and both mental and physical health benefits; and

 
WHEREAS, Maine's sportsmen and women were among the first conservationists to support the establishment of the Maine Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife to conserve fish, wildlife and their habitat, and through their license fees helped fund state efforts to provide for healthy and sustainable natural resources; and


WHEREAS, upon realizing that license fees alone were insufficient to restore and sustain healthy fish and wildlife populations, sportsmen and women supported self-imposed excise taxes on firearms and ammunition, fishing tackle and motorboat fuels to raise additional conservation funds; and


WHEREAS, to this day, the Maine Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife is funded, in part, by sportsmen and women, through this American System of Conservation Funding – a “user pays - public benefits” approach that is widely recognized as the most successful model for funding fish and wildlife management in the world; and


WHEREAS, last year alone, Maine's sportsmen and women generated $32 million through this system to support the conservation efforts of the Maine Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife; and


WHEREAS, 548,194 hunters and anglers support the state's economy through their spending, contributing to the $3.9 billion spent on outdoor activities in Maine last year; 


NOW THEREFORE, be it resolved that I, Janet T. Mills, Governor of the State of Maine, do hereby proclaim September 26, 2026 as 

National Hunting and Fishing Day

in Maine, and I urge all citizens to recognize the many and varied social, cultural, economic, and ecological benefits of our time-honored traditions of hunting and angling.

Ovarian Cancer Awareness Month

Hello, this is Governor Janet Mills, and thank you for listening.

You know, one of the great privileges of serving as your Governor is working with so many veterans to make sure they have all the opportunities that they deserve in our state. Our state is proud that we have one of the highest number of veterans per capita of any state in the country. And we're here to serve them.

I am proud to have the benefit of a number of veterans in my Administration, including members of the Cabinet like Commissioner Randy Liberty, Commissioner Mike Sauschuck, Commissioner and Adjutant General Diane Dunn, as well as a wonderful group of Aide de Camp who advised me and my Administration on issues relating to veterans.

I also come from a proud military family. Two uncles who fought in the Pacific in World War II. My brother who served three tours of duty in Vietnam, and my father who served in the Pacific during World War II at the Battle of Leyte Gulf. So I know that when our friends and family members come home from serving on the front lines, they deserve every opportunity to find rewarding careers in the civil sector that utilize their extensive skills, diverse experiences, and their unique training.

Maine's Hire-A-Vet Campaign is a key part of expanding those opportunities. The campaign had ambitious goals last year: 100 days, 100 employers, and 100 veterans hired. And thanks to everyone’s hard work, we achieved those goals, and we place veterans in good-paying jobs in every county in Maine. The employers hiring the most veterans included the State of Maine itself, Bonney Staffing, Northern Light Health, and Bath Iron Works.

Since its inception in 2015, the Hire-A-Vet Campaign has connected more than 2,000 employers with over 2,200 veterans hired. That's incredible.

And to all the businesses who helped make that happen, I say thank you. You folks hired Maine veterans because you recognized what we all know to be true. Veterans know what it means to work as a team and to leave no one behind. They know how to serve with integrity and commitment to a mission while adapting to dangers known and unknown. They have a great work ethic. That sounds like a pretty good employee to me.

Right now, skilled veterans have another chance to find high-quality jobs through our 2026 Hire-A-Vet Campaign. Once again, the goal of the campaign is to get at least 100 veterans hired by Maine employers within 100 days.

Whether you're a veteran returning to Maine or choosing Maine as your new home, or you're a longtime Maine resident making a career change or reentering the workforce, our Hire-A-Vet Campaign can help you with your job search. Just last month, nearly 50 employers participated in a virtual job fair, which included nearly 40 veterans and their family members. Some candidates attended from as far as Florida and Tennessee because, you know, Maine is where people want to be.

We have hiring fairs coming up in Bangor on September 24th, in Alfred on October 15th, and in Norway on November 12th. All jobseekers are invited.

The Maine Department of Labor also has Veterans’ Representatives located across the state year-round to serve you. I strongly encourage veterans who want to take the next step in their career to connect with a local Veterans’ Representative at one of the statewide CareerCenters. Both veterans and employers can also take advantage of the online CareerCenter at 207-623-7981 or at myworksourcemaine.gov.

My Administration will continue to partner with employers, big and small, through the Hire-A-Vet Campaign to make sure every veteran has the opportunity to live, work, and raise a family right here in Maine.

This is Governor Janet Mills, and thank you for listening.

item.title: Process for Authorizing Seasonal Migratory Game Bird Hunting — Federal Register — Documents Matching 'Maine'
item.description: The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service or we) is changing the administrative process for authorizing seasonal migratory game bird hunting in the United States. Migratory game bird hunting regulations are currently promulgated annually to provide opportunities for recreation and sustenance; aid Federal, State, and Tribal governments in the management of migratory game birds; and allow harvests at levels compatible with migratory game bird population status and habitat conditions. The Service is adopting a more efficient administrative process for authorizing seasonal migratory game bird hunting. The Service will issue a memorandum to establish the limits and authorize seasonal migratory game bird hunting once every 3 years. The Service will continue to make annual decisions on harvest levels and will update the memorandum sooner than 3 years if changes are prescribed by our decision frameworks. The process eliminates the need for subsequent annual Federal regulation promulgation and rulemaking and is expected to increase efficiency; better meet State, Tribal, and Federal rulemaking constraints; and reduce the complexity and costs. Our goal is to better serve State partners and the hunting public while continuing to meet the legal and conservation purposes of the Migratory Bird Treaty Act. Tribes are already authorized under a similar process.
